result.process_summary: Both the traffic‑light scenario and an if‑then statement involve evaluating a condition (sensor detection) and then performing one of two possible actions: a primary action when the condition holds (turn green) or an alternative/no action when it does not (stay red or activate a pedestrian signal). The causal flow—condition check → branch decision → action—is shared.
potential_breaks: Real traffic lights often follow timed cycles rather than purely condition‑driven changes.
A traffic light may consider multiple sensors or phases, whereas the analogy presents a single binary condition.
The ELSE example (pedestrian signal) assumes a mutually exclusive alternative that may not reflect typical else branches in code.
